A small desktop update for the Browser camera page: it can now turn the screen black while it streams, and it's a lot nicer to use sideways.

## New

**Black screen.** The new button on the page turns everything black while the camera keeps streaming. That saves battery and screen life on phones with an OLED screen. On Android it also goes full screen, so the status and navigation bars disappear too. Double tap to get the page back. A single tap only shows a hint with the connection status for a few seconds, so bumping the phone on its stand won't wake it. iPhones don't let web pages go full screen so there it opens a black video in the iPhone's own player instead, and closing the player brings the page back. This is an experimental workaround and I don't actually have an iPhone to test it on so please report any issues if you encounter them.

## Changed

- The buttons on the page got icons. Holding the phone sideways moves them to a column on the right, next to the preview instead of under it.
- The header on the page is gone to give the preview more room. The status dot now sits in front of the status line.
- If the phone drops the page's hold on keeping the screen on (battery saver can do that), the page asks for it again.

Browser camera works best in Chrome from my experience. Firefox works too but might stream in JPEG instead of H.264 and the aspect ratio of the camera is sometimes wrong.

The phone app has no changes in this release.

Found something broken? Open an issue and paste your **Copy diagnostics** report into it.
